sections.heading: Overview
content: According to the American Medical Association (AMA) Coding with Modifiers publication, “A physician may elect to terminate a surgical or diagnostic procedure due to extenuating circumstances or those that threaten the well-being of the patient. The discontinued procedure may be reported by adding modifier 53 to the code. Modifier 53 is only used for professional services.” This policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for services reported with modifier 53 .

sections.heading: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana requires a provider to report modifier 53 if the procedure is discontinued after anesthesia is administered. Modifier 53 should not be used for: • Evaluation and management codes • Facility claims • Charges for laparoscopic and endoscopic procedures converted to open procedures Humana will reject or deny a charge if modifier 53 is submitted inappropriately.

subsections.heading: Contracted Providers
content: If modifier 53 is appropriately appended to a service code, a Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plan allows 29 percent of the provider’s contracted rate. In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply.

subsections.heading: Noncontracted Providers
content: If modifier 53 is appropriately appended to a service code and that code has a modifier 53 -specific rate in the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS), a Humana MA plan allows the rate stated in the MPFS. If modifier 53 is appropriately appended to a service code and that code does not have a modifier 53 -specific rate in the MPFS, a Humana MA plan allows the service code's base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan , multiplied by the percentage of the service that was completed. For example, if 15 percent of the procedure was performed, then the plan allows 15 percent of the base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan for the service code. Humana requires a provider to submit medical records, including the operative report. In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply.

sections.heading: Kentucky Medicaid Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana requires a provider to report modifier 53 if the procedure is discontinued after anesthesia is administered. Modifier 53 should not be used for: • Evaluation and management codes • Facility claims • Charges for laparoscopic and endoscopic procedures converted to open procedures Humana will reject or deny a charge if modifier 53 is submitted inappropriately. If modifier 53 is appropriately appended to a service code, Humana allows: • 29 percent of the provider’s contracted rate; or • 29 percent of the base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan , if the provider is not contracted. Note: In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. For example, when applicable, claims are subject to the Humana Healthy Horizons in Kentucky out-of-network payment policy. For more information, see the relevant guidance in the References section of this policy.

sections.heading: Medicaid Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Except when a state-specific Medicaid section is outlined in this policy, Humana Medicaid plans follow state Medicaid guidelines, as applicable, regarding the reimbursement of a service code reported with modifier 53 .

sections.heading: Definitions of Italicized Terms
content: • Base maximum amount payable under the member’s plan: The maximum amount of reimbursement for a covered expense, determined by the member’s plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments. • Modifier 53: Discontinued procedure.

sections.heading: General Humana Resources
content: • Availity – Providers can register for access to information on a variety of topics such as eligibility, benefits, referrals, authorizations, claims and electronic remittances. • Claims processing edit notifications – Alerts of upcoming claims payment changes are posted on the first Friday of each month. • Claims resources – Providers can find information on referrals, authorizations, electronic claim submissions and more. • Making it easier – This page contains an educational series for providers and healthcare professionals. • Medical and pharmacy coverage policies – Humana publishes determinations of coverage of medical procedures, devices and medications for the treatment of various conditions. There may be variances in coverage among plans. • Publications – This page can help you find our quarterly newsletter, provider manual and other resources to help you do business with us.
